scope: Curated official documentation, not an API harvest or a verified working integration. Overlaps and gaps are questions for human review.

platforms.name: AI-on-Demand (AIoD)
platforms.description: European AI discovery, research and industry platform; AI4Europe and DeployAI contribute to it.

platforms.name: EOSC EU Node
platforms.description: European research resource and service federation with contributor onboarding.

platforms.name: AI4EOSC
platforms.description: Federated research AI modules, development, training and deployment.

platforms.name: EOSC-ARENA
platforms.description: EU-funded project extending AI4EOSC with agentic GenAI for science; planned capabilities must not be treated as deployed.

requirements.title: Find projects, tools and people
requirements.question: Can an agent discover relevant existing public research assets, projects, experts and source URLs?
requirements.acceptance: Return source-backed candidates with stable resource identities; compare with ordinary keyword search.

requirements.title: Spot duplicate work and reuse
requirements.question: Are independent teams solving the same requirement, and can one reuse a specific artifact?
requirements.acceptance: Name both requirements, implementation maturity, transferable artifact and technical mismatch; human confirms relevance.

requirements.title: Connect humans and agents
requirements.question: Can relevant humans/agents be notified and coordinate work across teams and systems?
requirements.acceptance: Show a consented, auditable cross-team handoff and whether participants were already coordinating.

requirements.title: Interoperable sources and services
requirements.question: Can a third-party catalogue, service, module or agent connect via documented APIs?
requirements.acceptance: Prove one end-to-end import/export with source and permission boundaries.

requirements.title: Shared model development and evaluation
requirements.question: Can separate contributors contribute to the same model-training or evaluation effort?
requirements.acceptance: Demonstrate one jointly versioned model/data/evaluation contribution and a reproducible outcome.

requirements.title: Provenance and verification
requirements.question: Can the platform track evidence, changes, dataset/model identity and human acceptance?
requirements.acceptance: Trace a suggestion to original sources and distinguish documentation, intentions and executed results.

observations.finding: Metadata Catalogue aggregates datasets, models, projects and papers from multiple sources; REST API and Python SDK are documented.

AIoD already has an open-source semantic catalogue search project (aiod-enhanced-interaction), including vector search. This is a strong retrieval baseline but does not establish requirement-level duplicate-work detection, artifact compatibility or new human collaborations.
Ecosystem mapping and RAIL support research collaboration; no cross-platform autonomous agent trigger protocol verified.
AIoD Metadata Catalogue has an official REST API and Python SDK, suitable for a future read-only adapter evaluation.
RAIL and the AI Builder support experiments; this does not establish a shared training pipeline for one common LLM.
Cross-platform metadata provides resource identities, not a verified provenance chain for our matcher's collaboration claims.
Resource Hub exposes research data, publications, software, services and related material from the federation.
Software and workflows can be found and reused, but documented discovery is not itself a duplicate-work detector.
Federated collaboration, shared services and access are documented, not automatic human-agent or agent-agent matching.
Contributor onboarding accepts eligible mature research tools, services and catalogues under review; not an unconditional publication API.
Compute and data services support research workflows; no EOSC-wide common LLM-training process is established by this source.
The federation emphasizes FAIR metadata, open research outputs and reproducible workflows; application-level claim verification is still separate.
Dashboard Marketplace lists reusable AI modules and related tools; narrower than general research-project discovery.
Reusable modules and common APIs support implementation reuse, not automated discovery of overlapping team requirements.
AI-module composition and common APIs exist, but the documented module infrastructure alone is not an agent-to-agent conversation network.
Modules expose a common API and can be deployed to local or federated resources; standard DEEPaaS integration is documented.
Platform supports training, fine-tuning, federated computing and shared modules; this does not imply joint training of one European foundation model.
Model-development and experiment-tracking services are documented; our particular cross-team evidence chain is not verified.
Research assistant is intended to cover literature review and knowledge-supported scientific workflows.
Planned agent marketplace and knowledge services may help reuse, but no implemented duplicate-work matcher is demonstrated.
Work package 6 explicitly plans composable agents and an agent-to-agent interoperability protocol; deliverables are still in preparation.
Project plans plug-in agent orchestration and interoperability integrated with EOSC and AI4EOSC.
Work package 7 covers scientific GenAI model pre- and post-training; this is not proof of a common open European foundation model.
Work package 8 plans data/model lifecycle tracking, provenance, persistent IDs and automatically generated metadata.

cross_project_cases.title: Model-card reporting / benchmark provenance
cross_project_cases.finding: OpenEuroLLM needs model-card reports; LAION has an optional audit-manifest proposal. Code compatibility and maintainer interest are not established.

cross_project_cases.title: 256k context extension / StateBench
cross_project_cases.finding: OpenEuroLLM's ongoing 256k model extension could potentially use AllenAI's merged long-context state-tracking evaluations; runner compatibility is unknown.

cross_project_cases.title: Arena-Hard v2 / contamination exclusion
cross_project_cases.finding: Both teams address Arena-Hard v2, but one implements pairwise scoring and the other cleans contaminated results. Neither duplicate code nor a transferable contract is proven.
